::: {#exr-find-mle}
#### Identifying the MLE

Draw conclusions about the MLE of $\rate$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-find-mle}

Since $\hess(\tilde \rate; \vx) < 0$,
$\tilde \rate$ is a local maximizer of the log-likelihood.
Moreover, $\hess(\rate; \vx) = -n\bar x/\rate^2 < 0$ for every $\rate > 0$,
so the log-likelihood is strictly concave,
and a local maximizer of a strictly concave function
is its unique global maximizer.
So $\tilde \rate$ maximizes $\llik$, and therefore $\Lik$:

```{r}
#| label: calc-mle
#| code-fold: false
mle <- mean(cyclones$number)
mle
```

$$
\ba
\hrate_{\text{ML}}
&= \bar x\\
&= `r round(mle, 3)`
\ea
$$

:::
